articleTitle: Performance Evaluation and Energy Management System for Parallel Hybrid Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Today, worldwide, there is large research work going on to develop hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) which relieve the nation from the dependence on fossil fuels like petrol, diesel and vehicles which do not pollute the atmosphere. To achieve this objective, HEVs using alternate fuel sources like fuel cells, batteries, capacitors, flywheels are used with an electric drive system. In some HEVs there are more than one drive system, like an electric drive system along with a conventional engine (ICE) based drive system. These drive systems are used in various combinations like series/parallel depending upon the design adopted. In this paper, it is proposed to evaluate the performance of existing and HEVs under development. Based on the study of the HEVs and their performance evaluation, it is proposed to develop an energy system with one or more power sources and an energy management and control sources (EMCS). The EMCS will effectively manage these power sources. These power sources will be tailor made to match a suitable drive system for an HEV. The drive system will be appropriately selected based on the above study. Simulation work is carried out using state-of-the-art software tools like MATLAB - SIMULINK. The simulation results will be validated by comparing with an appropriate baseline specification of HEV.

articleTitle: Hybrid Renewable Energy System Design and Optimization for Developing Countries Using HOMER Pro: Case of Rwanda
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: HOMER (Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewables) is a tool invented by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) used in renewable power systems optimization. This tool is utilized by researchers to design and model various power system and hybrid system configuration. HOMER has different built-in component and devices such as hydro turbines, PV modules, generators, batteries, converters, utility loads transformers and many more. Researchers are able to simulates different power systems designed by HOMER and also find the most optimized power system configurations considering the operating cost, the net present cost, the carbon oxide emission and comparison of economic viability. Currently the energy demand is highly increasing worldwide therefore the design and implementation of new renewable energy systems with zero gas emission is needed for the future energy forecasting and pollution free energy systems implementation to reduce the dependence on conventional energies. This work modeled a hybrid system for Gicumbi district in Rukomo village in which the designed system deals with solar, wind and converters to decrease amount of electricity paid to the national grid. This work evaluates the power generated, emitted gases, net present cost and the cost of electricity. The work presents various optimized system simulated results. The proposed hybrid wind-PV system scheme is generalized to the most economic comparing to other systems considering the operating cost, the NPC and the toxic gases emission.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy Systems Considering Stepped Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Under the background of “double carbon”, an integrated energy system (IES) low-carbon economic operation strategy is proposed to improve energy utilization and further reduce the carbon emission level of the IES. Firstly, the carbon trading mechanism is introduced into the IES, and a stepped carbon trading calculation model is constructed to divide the carbon emission interval. Then, the carbon absorption characteristics of Power-to-Gas (P2G) access are considered, and the incentive mechanism for P2G to participate in carbon market trading is allowed to improve the actual carbon emission model. Finally, the low-carbon economic operation objectives and constraints are constructed to minimize the energy purchase cost, carbon emission cost, and abandoned wind penalty cost. By setting up several scheduling scenarios for analysis, the effectiveness of the carbon trading mechanism developed in this paper in the operation of the IES low-carbon economy is verified.

articleTitle: Design of Fuzzy Controller for a Hybrid Active/Passive Cooling System in Smart Homes with a Windcatcher
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Globally, most building energy consumption is associated with heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems (HVAC). Building energy consumption increased from 115 EJ in 2010 to nearly 135 EJ in 2021, accounting for 30% of global final energy consumption. In 2021, electricity will account for approximately 35% of building energy use, up from 30% in 2010. Space cooling, in particular, saw the greatest increase in demand across all building end uses in 2021, increasing by more than 6.5% over 2020. This study aims to set design guidelines to reduce energy consumption in building sector by proposing a hybrid active/passive cooling smart system. This can reduce energy consumed by the electricity grid by achieving natural ventilation through wind catchers. The later is a historical architectural element used in buildings to provide cross ventilation and passive cooling. The architectural modeling of the proposed system's design is conducted using Autodesk Revit. The smart controlling system is implemented with Fuzzy logic in MATLAB Simulink. Moreover, the accuracy of the system is improved by a PID tuning based on Backpropagation Neural Network. The results confirmed the effectiveness of the methodology used.

articleTitle: Simulation of Transient Overvoltage Under Different Operation Modes of Disconnectors in 500 kV Pumped Storage Power Station
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In order to calculate and analyze the VFTO (ultra-fast transient overvoltage) and influencing factors of 500kV GIS Substation of a pumped storage power station when the motor is operated by disconnector at different positions under the mode of generator and motor operation, the circuit simulation model is established by using EMTP-ATP electromagnetic transient program. The analysis results show that the VFTO amplitude generated during the operation of the disconnector at the main transformer side is large, and the VFTO amplitude generated during the operation of the disconnector at the line side is the smallest. At the same time, the operation of disconnectors at different positions has little impact on the VFTO signal strength, but has a great impact on the VFTC (ultra-fast transient current) transient signal.

articleTitle: Efficiency Comparison of 2-Level and 3-Level Si IGBT Based Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In this study, an experimental study of a 20 kVA 2-level neutral point inverter and a 3-level diode-clamped inverter has been carried out under 4 different linear loads. At the end of the experimental study, oscilloscope images obtained under 4 different loads were shared. The efficiency of the 2-level neutral point inverter and the 3-level diode clamped inverter under 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% linear loads were measured with a power analyzer. The efficiency comparison results of the 2-Level and 3-Level inverter are shared.

articleTitle: Passive Cooling with Finned Roof Tiles
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Cooling load demands have increased rapidly over the recent years. In extreme hot climates, the building sector consumes more than 90% of the total electricity of the country. Thermal comfort can however be improved by using passive cooling techniques. One of these methods is the cool roof approach. Two identical cabins were designed and constructed in Kuwait to test different cool roof techniques. In this study, a new system was proposed by using aluminum sheet tiles equipped with tilted fins to minimize direct sun light in the roof and reduce its temperature. Hourly temperatures and humidity were monitored for both units along with the power consumption of air conditioning, if required. The initial data shows nearly identical thermal properties of both units. The results were shown for two months of winter in Kuwait and the study will continue for other months of the year with more improvements, like using reflective paint or spacers between the tiles and the roof.

articleTitle: A Study on Damping Controller for Grid-Forming Inverter Power Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The application of grid-forming inverter(GFM) that can control voltage and frequency similar to synchronous generators is a key for a weak grid with a high penetration level of renewable energy sources (RES). However, the GFM connected to the high short circuit ratio(SCR) power system can cause instability in the synchronization process. This is because the closer the electrical distance is, the more sub-synchronous oscillation occurs in GFM. Therefore, GFM operation may not be possible due to oscillation occurrence and control instability when GFM is initially integrated into high SCR. In this paper, to get the mechanism of GFM which is unstable control according to SCR, we propose a basic structure of GFM small model. A small-signal model of GFM based on droop control with a SISO system that reduces the coupling of current and voltage has been utilized for the stability analysis. Through controller stability analysis, we proved that the unstable pole point of GFM at high SCR and that controller converges to a stable condition when the proposed damping control is applied to the existing droop control. The verification of the proposed damping control method and approach has been performed by using the electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Real-Time Solar Irradiation Monitoring and Forecasting Application for PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Due to the high penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs), especially, solar power or photovoltaic (PV), the operation of the power system has coped with several severe technical issues such as supply-demand balance and low inertia. To mitigate these problems, PV power generation or solar irradiance forecast is of great importance. In the last decades, myriad forecasting methods have been introduced, yet these approaches do not concentrate on the real-time forecast. This paper proposes deep learning-based real-time solar irradiation monitoring and forecasting system with data collected from sensors before being stored in the database. Two predictive models, namely, Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) and Convolution Neural Network - Long Short-term Memory (CNN-LSTM), are constructed for day-ahead solar irradiance forecasting. These predicted results are aggregated employing Linear Least Square (LLS) method into the selected forecast values and updated periodically. The forecasting results show that the selected predicting values improve significantly compared to individual ones.

articleTitle: WPT Resonant Frequency Design Considerations for Electrical Vehicle Dynamic Charging Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents the work to evaluate the power efficiency performance of a DC/DC series-series resonates converter at different resonant frequencies for electrical vehicle dynamic charging applications. A power loss breakdown study is performed in PLECS circuit simulation to identify the components contributing to significant power loss. The simulation and measurement results are compared for both alignment and misalignment operation conditions for three resonant frequencies at 45 kHz, 65 kHz, and 85 kHz. The effect of the operation frequency on wireless charging system efficiency and performance is analyzed for dynamic EV charging applications. From the analytical calculation and experimental study, the conclusion is made that operating DC/DC converter at a high resonant frequency can significantly improve the power transfer efficiency and power output capability of the wireless charging system at the misaligned position in the dynamic EV wireless charging process.

articleTitle: Extract Power-line Key Points From LiDAR Data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The power-line point cloud obtained by LiDAR can represent 3D geometric information of power lines, which has important applications in power line inspection. However, the rapid growth of point cloud data has brought challenges to data transmission, storage, and processing. An alternative approach is to preserve the structural information of relevant objects from point cloud data. This structure information is also useful in some important tasks, such as obstacle troubleshooting and sag measurement. In this paper, we aim to extract power-line key points from LiDAR data to represent the power-line structure. Unlike most existing methods that use 3D line fitting, we propose a data-driven approach that exploits point features in the 2D plane and 3D space. Our method first projects 3D points onto a 2D plane, which can largely reflect the distribution of points. It then uses the local features of points to extract power-line key points. We demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method using an original data set consisting of 50 power-line point clouds. The results show that our method is intuitive, easy to understand, and suitable for practical applications.

articleTitle: EDLC Modeling Based on Charge Redistribution Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The charge redistribution phenomenon is a memory effect exhibited by supercapacitors, which always draws close to the charge state at the previous moment, which makes many supercapacitor energy storage systems have obvious voltage changes during the stationary process, affecting the control strategy or causing the calculated energy storage efficiency to decrease, and may even endanger the safety of operators. In order to effectively simulate the charge redistribution phenomenon at different resting times, this paper firstly introduces the charge redistribution principle of supercapacitor from a microscopic perspective, and then proposes an optimization method of supercapacitor branching model according to this phenomenon, which can select the number of branches according to the working conditions and improve the computational efficiency of the model.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator Control Implementation in Single-stage Solar Energy Conversion System for Transient Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) has been developed in the past few decades to address the problem of transient dynamics, i.e. primary control, virtual inertia. Many researchers use DC voltage sources or neglect MPPT controller in VSG studies. It leaves a research gap whereas the DC voltage source is an infinite source where in solar PV system, the power is limited and affected by MPPT controller. This paper investigates the VSG implementation in single-stage solar energy conversion system (SECS) interconnected to an aggregated weak grid condition. This paper presents a feasible way to implement VSG in a practical application without compromising MPPT performance.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Interturn Short Circuit Using Repetitive Surge Oscillograph
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that it is difficult to detect the slight interturn short circuit fault of transformer windings, this paper proposes to use the repetitive surge oscillograph to diagnose the interturn short circuit fault. By analyzing the propagation process of pulse signal in transformer winding, a distributed parameter circuit model of transformer winding is established to reflect the propagation process, and the variation law of wave impedance after interturn short circuit is deduced. By inputting a low-voltage pulse at one end of the transformer winding and collecting the response characteristic curve at the other end, the characteristic curve is obtained by combining the two response characteristic curves before and after the interturn short circuit of the winding. Analyze whether the characteristic curve protrudes to judge whether interturn short circuit fault occurs, so as to realize fault diagnosis. The degree of protrusion of the characteristic curve reflects the severity of winding short circuit fault, and then analyze its identification degree in combination with artificial neural network algorithm.

articleTitle: A real-time experimental investigation of thin cambered tubercle blades for performance improvement of Darrieus vertical axis wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Darrieus vertical axis wind turbines (VAWT) have various shapes associated with them; H-shaped devices are amongst the most common designs being used. To enhance the performance of these devices, nature-inspired tubercle shapes have been implemented to these H-shaped blade profiles. Hump-back whale flippers inspire these tubercles. They have a sinusoidal pattern on the flippers, which has been stated to help these gigantic beings to have sharp turns. The present study has implemented this modification to the H-bladed profile. A NACA4412 profile has been selected for the present study. An experimental analysis has been performed with three-bladed turbines with modified shape in a subsonic wind tunnel having a straight cambered and cambered tubercle. The tubercle model outperforms the straight-cambered models. The analysis was performed at wind speeds of 6 to 7 m/s to mimic the natural wind flow operating conditions. Real-time torque data were plotted using a rotary torque sensor for 100 sec of operation. The tubercle model showed a 16.66% increase in increment in the torque value at 7 m/s.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Multidimensional Components for the Diagnosis of Faults in Electric Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The current manufacturing technification has resulted in business competitiveness because their products might be customized in some cases, the reason to understand that the production line should not stop in the presence of possible mechanical or electronic failures. Against this background and knowing that approximately 80% of the induction motors operate in the industrial sector, a maintenance record or control should be kept due to its direct relationship with production. With this perspective, various studies attempt to diagnose a type of incipient failure that may occur, traditional and/or robust. Thus, this document employs the multidimensional technique or Park demodulation, to perform an analysis in three case studies, the Park Vector Module (PVM) and each constituted component (1<inf>a</inf> and I<inf>d</inf>). These failures will be identified using statistical tools, analyzing their behavior and indications that reveal a diagnosis in the presence of possible incipient failures; in addition, these results will be helpful for those studies that involve probability or artificial intelligence topics for preventive or predictive diagnoses. Results show that there is evidence for the identification of different types of incipient failures, depending on the type of tool and the analysis case; specifically, one type of failure is identified for the standard deviation, three for box plots and ambiguity generation for the correlation coefficient; however, four types of failures proposed for this case study are identified for the quadratic mean.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Active Equalization Control of Dynamical Systems in Hybrid Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Millions of aircrafts take off and land at airports every day, and aircrafts consume a lot of fuel during the flight, which leads to resource shortages and environmental pollutions. The sudden and successful application of new energy vehicles have promoted the development of aircrafts in the direction of new energy and using new energy to drive aircraft and maintain the safe and stable flight of aircraft is an urgent issue to be solved. This paper proposes a modular model of the power system of a hybrid aircraft, analyzes the energy consumption in the power system based on the Boeing 737–800, calculates the energy ratio of the battery pack, and reserves the modular accessed method of new energy sources such as solar energy and nuclear energy. A sample set weighted random forest decision function classification model is proposed, and a dynamical system equilibrium control model is designed. The theoretical analysis results show that based on ensuring the safety and stability of the aircraft, the hybrid aircrafts will consume less resources than the fuel aircrafts during the cruise, thereby reducing environmental pollution and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Shallow Geothermal and Solar Energy-Driven Adsorption-Compression Hybrid Air Conditioning System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Adsorption chillers can be driven by solar thermal energy or waste heat which is considered an important air-conditioning system in net zero buildings. Traditional adsorption chillers operate with solar thermal energy at 50°C and a cooling tower at 33 °C, but the energy efficiency is too low. The chilling water only achieved 18--20°C at this operating condition. The authors used a shallow geothermal energy system with a temperature of 22°C to replace the cooling tower. The coefficient of performance of the adsorption chiller can increase from 0.18 to 0.4. Two types of adsorption-compression hybrid systems are developed according to different seasons. Mode A uses solar thermal energy to drive the adsorption chiller for cold storage and reduces the load of the compression chiller at night. Mode B produces 16°C chilling water and cooling the condenser of the compression chiller; this can significantly improve the efficiency of the compressor by 22%. Because the essential construction components of a villa-type green building already include shallow geothermal energy and solar thermal energy, the estimated minimum payback period of the hybrid system is 2.1 years.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Electricity Consumption Using Neural Networks in Public Hospital Buildings with Installed Smart Meters in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Thailand has promoted the national plan for energy consumption to achieve a target of the reduction of energy intensity by 30 percent in 2030. Therefore, energy conservation measures have been taken in the designated buildings particularly. For designated public hospital buildings in particular, electricity use contributes the most part of energy consumption and gradually increases every year. Therefore, this paper aims to strengthen the energy efficiency plan by forecasting electricity demand from smart meters using a recurrent neural network (RNN) model. This model is developed from the acquired dataset from over 2,100 installed smart meters. It was found that the RNN model could be used for a long-term prediction of electricity consumption with acceptable results based on the limited dataset for public hospital buildings. The study also examined the model on three scales of sample hospital buildings, which are large, medium, and small scale. The result revealed that a trend of prediction is according to actual consumption. Moreover, the accuracy of the forecast model is evaluated by the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and mean square error (MSE) methods, and the MAPE has lower than 20 percent.

articleTitle: Pilot Evaluation of a Low Cost Fully Mechanical Solar Tracker Using Swiss Lever Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Although solar energy has become the primary source of increasing access to electricity in rural areas, espe-cially for developing nations, maximising their efficiency with a tracking system is still widely discouraged. Furthermore, current tracking system designs are inconsiderate of end-user capabilities. This paper presents the pilot evaluation of a mechanical tracking system, designed to be fabricated with a wide range of material choices and allow utilisation irrespective of user skill. The tracker uses a fully mechanical system to rotate at a fixed speed, maintained by a swiss lever mechanism. Pilot evaluation shows a 28.65% possible increase in energy generation during peak solar hours.

articleTitle: Making Power Systems Sustainable with Natural Ester Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the pressing need of having to meet continuous rising demand for electricity and having to cope with the rapid deployment of distributed renewable energy sources, utilities are striving to explore ways to drive economic and environmental sustainability in their operations. As one of the most critical equipment in power systems, transformers are key to delivering an agile and robust power supply against overloading and against the intermittent nature of renewable energy [1]. Due to the possibility of having additional loading capacity beyond the rated load at normal temperature rise limit using natural ester dielectric fluid to replace mineral oil in the insulation systems, the paradigm of having to match the transformer's rated capacity to the expected peak demand can be shifted. Drawing on proven industrial practices and key findings from extensive case studies, this paper reviews different ways of utilizing the higher loading capacity and flexibility in natural ester-filled transformers. It also discusses how end users can select the most viable option based on their applications to deliver tangible sustainability and total cost of ownership benefits through prolonged equipment life and improved energy and material efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of Corrosion in Carbon Steel Pipeline of Marine Wastewater Outfall during Electric Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Municipal wastewater is discharged into the sea after undergoing adequate/suitable treatment process. Carbon steel pipes are the most commonly used subsea metal pipes to transport wastewater deep under the sea. These carbon steel pipes experience corrosion which leads to an increased surface roughness. Pipe surface roughness determines the pressure losses as a result of the friction during the flow of fluid within the pipeline. Hence, pressure losses lead to a reduction in fluid volumetric flow rate. At the outlet of the carbon steel pipeline, a significant amount of energy can be generated from discharged wastewater. It can be generated using hydrokinetic turbine coupled to a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG). Hence, the aim of this paper is to investigate the potential impact of corrosion formation within the carbon steel pipe during electric power generation. MATLAB/Simulink tool has been used to develop the model. Hence, different absolute roughness's have been modelled to analyse the potential impact. When the absolute roughness is increased from 44 micro meters to 60 micro meters, this has led to a 0.44% decrease in generated voltage. Hence, both the rotational speed and frequency of the PMSG were also reduced by 5.4% and 3.6%, respectively.

articleTitle: Shut-down Strategy of PEMFC Power System Based on Pulse Current Control Method
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) power system operates under a variety of conditions due to changes in load demand, among which the shutdown process and shutdown state are the key factors that affect the system's health state and economics. Therefore, it is of great significance to explore a reasonable shutdown strategy for the healthy and reliable operation of the system. In this paper, a pulse current control method is proposed to release the residual energy and maintain the system shutdown state within the range of low voltage and safe pressure during the shutdown process, in view of the cell voltage and pressure operation characteristics and the ideal state requirements for cell voltage and pressure during the shutdown process. The method is crucial for the power system to swiftly maintain the ideal state during a short or long downtime through mechanism and data model simulation of reactant supply, and the analysis of shutdown test experiments.

articleTitle: Application of Park's Vector and Current Envelope Method for Diagnosis of Stator Winding Inter Turn Fault of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents a new efficient approach to analyse the inter turn stator winding fault in three phase induction motors. The proposed procedure is experimentally studied for normal and faulty cases of test motor at different loading conditions. Motor current signature analysis method is used along with stator current signature analysis methods namely park vectors and current envelope analysis which helps to extract the important information from the three-phase stator current signature. Statistical parameters are calculated of time domain from the each extracted signals. These computed statistical parameters strategy is able to distinguish between healthy and faulty conditions of test motor effectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient Scalogram Generator for Partial Shading Analysis of Photovoltaic Array
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems are negatively affected by many troubles, such as conductor faults, broken glass, cell aging, etc. Among them, partial shading conditions (PSC) not only reduce the output power of the PV systems but also cause hot spots on the surface of PV panels. This paper presents a Convolutional Neural Network-based method for PSC detection and classification. The highlights of this proposal are a scalogram extracted from the I-V characteristics of the PV array and a preprocessing phase implemented by a periodic function-based filter and the wavelet transform. The best accuracy of the proposed model is 98.41% through 819 test images after 50 training epochs, which proves its effectiveness. The future improvement of this work is also discussed in the conclusions.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT Based Photovoltaic Monitoring System Using Hybrid Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This research outlines the design, implementation, and testing of a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) based photovoltaic (PV) monitoring system which hybridizes physical modeling and machine learning. The physical models solve for preliminary expectations for PV power generation, while the machine learning model is applied to account for additional system inefficiencies. The proposed monitoring system consists of a Raspberry Pi as the central computing unit and several sensors to collect environmental data. In this research, a hardware system was created, including a mock PV system and the proposed monitoring system. A software system was developed as well, to implement the hybrid modeling of the expected power and compare it with the actual generated power to detect anomalies. The proposed monitoring system can accurately compute the expected power generation of PV systems and effectively detect anomalies which cause power losses. Results from the system find that the monitoring system with hybrid modeling has good performance, as the residual difference between the expected and actual measured power is within 2%, regardless of weather conditions. The average residual difference is 0.74% and the average Mean Absolute Error between the expected and actual measured power is 0.31 for the testing period, which is more accurate than either physical or machine learning modeling alone.

articleTitle: A Rapid Model Prediction Control Method for T- Type Three-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The three-level inverter island operation control system adopts the finite set model prediction control. During optimization, 27 voltage vectors need to be traversed and optimized. At the same time, the secondary control of the midpoint potential is needed in the optimization process, and the coefficient selection of capacitive voltage prediction term is related to the load. Transforming the load also requires additional calculations for the coefficients, resulting in complex and time-consuming operations. Aiming at these two problems, this paper proposes a fast model prediction method for T-type three-level inverter island operation, which reduces the 27 switch vectors in the finite control set to 3 switch vectors and reduces the amount of calculation in the control process. Using the redundant small vector for the midpoint potential, the cost function of a single output current is proposed, which avoids the difficulty of selecting the coefficients of the midpoint potential term. Finally, thanks to simulation and analysis, the validity of the theoretical analysis and the proposed control strategy is checked.

articleTitle: Minimum Capacity of Wind and Solar Energy Considering the Expansion of Hydro Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The pressure of low-carbon development drives the further integration of wind turbine (WT), photovoltaic units (PV) and hydro plants. The WT, PV and hydro plants in a certain area should be considered together as they have stong correlation. This paper proposes a two-stage stochastic programming model for the capacity planning of WT and PV in a hydro power system. The first stage is the capacity investment on the WT and PV while the second stage is the operation of power system considering hydro constraints. The scenarios in the stochastic programming are extracted from historical data. The model is in the mixed-integer bilinear formulation and solved by an iterative trial-and-error method. A power system in Southwest China is adapted as the test system. Different cases include the expansion of normal hydro plant (NHP), pumped storage hydro plant (PSHP) and NHP plus PSHP are considered. The results demonstrate that the NHP is more effective in reducing the capacity of WT and PV and the curtailment decreases with the integration of hydro plants.

articleTitle: Research on Operation and Maintenance Mode of Digital Substation Based on Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The digital substation is an important part of the new power system, and it is a modern substation for information sharing and interoperability between intelligent electrical equipment in the substation. In the context of the further increase in the technical complexity of equipment and the stricter requirements for operation and maintenance management, it has become very important to formulate an efficient operation and maintenance management model. This paper firstly analyzes the main problems existing in the operation and maintenance of digital substations, and clarifies the requirements of operation and maintenance management. Secondly, the evaluation index system of the operation and maintenance management mode is established. Then, the applicability of various operation and maintenance modes is analyzed by using the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process. Evaluation and calculation, according to the calculation results, the optimal selection scheme is obtained, which provides a new idea for improving the operation and maintenance management level of digital substations under the new power system.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control and Battery Energy Storage System Based Power System Secondary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The battery energy storage system (BESS) can quickly supplement the power demand of the power load and absorb the peak power generated by new energy. Therefore, the installed capacity of the BESS in the power system continues to increase, and it has been more and more widely used in the frequency modulation control of the power system. A fuzzy logic based control method for BESS to participate in power system frequency regulation control is proposed. The area control error (ACE) signal and the state of charge (SOC) of the energy storage battery are used as control inputs, thus the frequency regulation demand determined by ACE signal and the SOC limit of the energy storage battery are integrated to realize both health management of the energy storage battery and the frequency regulation control of the power grid.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Control Method of Three-Phase Load Imbalance Considering Distributed Photovoltaic Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The distribution power system, as the terminal link between the power system and the customer connection, still suffers from asymmetric three-phase line parameters and three-phase load imbalance. At present, the three-phase imbalance management method is still incomplete and does not take into account the extensive usage of distributed power sources. Therefore, a complete set of three-phase imbalance management methods considering the distributed power sources is urgently needed. In this paper, a comprehensive three-phase load imbalance governance method considering distributed PV power is proposed. Firstly, the UMAP dimensionality reduction method and the K-means clustering method are used to identify of consumer-phase relationship under the station area. After that, with the lowest three-phase imbalance as the goal, the genetic algorithm is used to optimize the phase of users and complete the three-phase imbalance governance. Finally, the results of the case analysis show that the proposed method can achieve accurate three-phase imbalance management in the distributed power access scenario considering distributed photovoltaic generation.

articleTitle: A Comparison on Energy Benchmarks of Designated Public University Buildings in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Three energy benchmarks, i.e., Specific Energy Consumption (SEC), Energy Utilization Index (EUI) and Energy Performance Indicator (EnPI), were investigated for assessment of energy consumption in twenty-three designated public university buildings in Thailand. Advantages and limitations of these benchmarks were reviewed. Among the three energy benchmarks, the SEC is more convenient to be used since all required data are readily available for use. However, the SEC must be used for its own sector. Actual energy consumption of these buildings was compared with the EUI baseline energy consumption. The EUI equation was developed based on the 2007 energy consumption data. The EnPI used the up-to-date data from the building energy auditing. It is imperative that several parameters must be sufficiently collected to establish the EnPI baseline energy consumption. To establish energy benchmarks properly, policymakers need to understand which benchmark is suitable as an indicator for energy consumption for each building.

articleTitle: Effects of Particulate Matter Pollution in Predicting Solar Radiation: A Case Study of Eastern Cape, South Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Increasing air pollution reduces surface solar radiation, making it one of the most important factors when estimating monthly global solar radiation (MGSR). The artificial intelligence techniques (artificial neural networks and support vector regression) were compared in this study to ascertain which of the particulate matter has greater effect on the prediction of solar radiation in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. The artificial intelligence models were trained using monthly data from January 1990 to September 2011 and tested using data from October 2011 to December 2020. The data was analyzed using statistical methods such as mean absolute percentage error, coefficient of correlation, and coefficient of determination. It can be concluded that incorporating the sea salt mass concentration of <tex>$\mathbf{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> yielded a better precision when estimating the MGSR in Eastern Cape of South Africa.

articleTitle: Research on the Development Status of Electric Energy Storage at Home and Abroad from the Perspective of Standardization
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Energy storage is an important technology and basic equipment for building a new type of power system. The healthy development of the energy storage industry cannot be separated from the support of standardization. With the adjustment of the national energy policy and the implementation of the energy conservation and environmental protection policy, the application scale of the energy storage technology in China is gradually expanding, which inevitably puts forward new requirements for standardization. Through the research on the standardization of electric energy storage at home and abroad, combined with the development needs of the energy storage industry, this paper analyzes the future development focus of the standardization of electric energy storage, and gives suggestions to promote the development of electric energy storage technology from the perspective of standardization, providing technical guidance and strong guarantee for the industrialization development of the energy storage industry and key areas of future development.

articleTitle: Decentralized Droop Control Strategies for Parallel-Connected Distributed Generators in an AC Islanded Microgrid: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper reviews the different decentralized droop control strategies in an AC microgrid. Microgrids are made up of parallel-connected distributed generators (DGs), storage devices and loads operating with coordinated control. They often integrate Renewable Energy Sources (RES) as DGs. The grid can operate in grid-connected and autonomous modes. Due to the intermittent nature of RES, the imbalance between power demand and power supply, the presence of different types of loads and line impedance mismatch, effective sharing of active and reactive power, as well as the regulation of frequency and voltage become imperative in the islanded mode of operation in order to ensure system stability. Droop control is preferred over other control strategies for sharing active and reactive power because it does not require communication channels. This paper review presents the merits and demerits of decentralized droop control methods. Furthermore, possible suggestions for improvement on active and reactive power sharing for parallel-connected DGs are presented including voltage and frequency regulation in an AC islanded microgrid.

articleTitle: Design, Modeling of a Green Building Energy Optimized Efficient System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Traditional buildings waste a large amount of energy and generate significant amounts of carbon dioxide (CO2), approximately 40% in the developed world and 33% elsewhere. Traditional buildings have been built for years without considering being given to their impact on global warming. Since 1973, simulation of green buildings (GB) has started in many countries; in particular, the US has shown a positive response to minimize the usage of energy. Consequently, software companies have developed efficient simulation software to interface interoperability with building information Modeling (BIM). The last decade has witnessed a rapidly growing number of studies on GB energy-efficient systems. However, the study also indicated that the results of the current GB simulation are not yet satisfactory for meeting the objectives of GB. In addition, most of these previous studies were unlikely exclude studies on optimized building energy efficiency simulations. The aim of this study is to meet the objectives of GB by the design, modeling, and simulation of building optimized energy efficiency systems. Thus, this study presents a multilevel, L-shaped office building in which every part of the building material has been tested for energy efficiency. Hence, A total of 78.62% energy is saved, approaching NetZero energy saving.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study and Cost Analysis of Electrification for a Non-electrified Railway Line
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The strong environmental commitment is pushing rapidly towards a complete de-carbonisation of industrial processes. The energy market is in continuous evolution, especially in the most recent years, with always increasing energy costs. This influences also the transportation sector. The aim of this paper is to provide a feasibility study and cost analysis regarding the whole electrification process of an already existing railway line. This work wants to analyse in details the process from the point of view of the railway owner. In particular, a focus is set on installation and maintenance costs of the electrical traction system and the evaluation of the investment payback time, depending on the potential increase in passengers per day. The analysis helps to understand how the situation of the framework will evolve in few decades from now, according to some assumptions. Finally, some Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are identified, and their comparison is used to assess the best alternatives. Two already existing non-electrified railway lines in Italy have been considered as case studies, located in Northern Italy, which are Pavia - Casalpusterlengo and Parma - San Zeno.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Electro-Heating Energy with the Participation of an Energy Hub
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: There are various risks in the integrated electro-heating system with the uncertainty of source and load. This paper constructs a fuzzy optimization scheduling model of integrated electro-heating system with the participation of an energy hub for studying the operation optimization problem of integrated electro-heating system caused by the uncertainty of sources and loads. Firstly, the integrated electro-heating system model with the participation of an energy hub is established. Secondly, fuzzy opportunity constraints of the uncertainty of source and load are introduced, and a fuzzy opportunity constraint model of lower layer credibility considering the uncertainty of wind power, electricity and heat load is established. Finally, the model of lower layer is processed in a clear equivalence manner. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Mitigating the Challenge of Energy Crisis via Energy Audit and Efficiency Measures: A Case of a Household in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Approximately 90 million of Nigeria's residents are without electricity access; this represents 12.5% of the world's population without access. Nigeria is challenged in meeting goal 7 of the sustainable development goals (SDGs) due to inadequate power generation to meet demands, poor transmission networks and insufficient investment. Proposing energy audits and efficiency measures, such as proper housekeeping, retrofitting electrical systems and installing renewable energy sources, will help reduce energy consumption and mitigate the country's energy crisis. This study conducted on a residential building in Nigeria found that retrofitting the building lighting system could achieve annual savings of as much as 230kWh and have a payback period of 9 months with a return on investment (ROI) of 126%. The retrofit of the pump system is expected to save 182kWh within a payback period of 2 years and have an ROI of 50%. The installation of solar panels and retrofit of batteries is expected to save 3MWh at a capital cost of N300,000, with an ROI of 26% and a net present value of over N690,000. These measures would also reduce a total of 1.97 tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimal Configuration Model of RIES with Biogas, Photovoltaic, and Wind
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Economy and environmental protection are two key factors in the planning of integrated energy system (IES). The existing collaborative optimal configuration method of IES considering both economy and environmental protection has a problem with a single configuration scheme and the unbalanced weight of economy and environmental protection in the configuration scheme. In this paper, a rural integrated energy system (RIES) with biogas, photovoltaic, and wind is proposed, and its collaborative optimal configuration model is constructed. In the upper-level configuration optimization model, a multi-objective optimization method based on the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II(NSGA-II) to obtain the Pareto optimal solution set is used to establish two objective functions that meet the economic and environmental requirements respectively. The optimal configuration scheme set is obtained by taking the minimum sum of annual total costs as the economic objective and the minimum carbon emissions as the environmental protection objective. In the lower-level optimal operation model, based on the configuration scheme obtained from the upper level, the optimal operation cost is obtained and fed back to the upper level with the objective of minimizing the annual operation cost (including pollutant treatment cost and carbon emission cost). The simulation results showed that, compared with the two-level single objective optimization method and the weight analysis method, the proposed collaborative optimal configuration method can provide users with more diversified and refined decision-making schemes and the optimal configuration scheme with the same objective requirements.

articleTitle: The Application Study on Solar Photovoltaic Technology in the Ocean Park Design
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: First of all, the marine ocean design focuses on practical value, then satisfies the design and construction of human landscape and lastly complies with environmental concerns. This paper considers some inherent forms like public buildings with sustainable solar installations in harmony with the urban landscape, puts forward the basic principles of reducing decorative elements, improving structural safety and efficiency, and presents the details the theory of color, color and material. This reflects the unique form of the building and reduces the decorative elements so that the form is integrated into the building. In the installation of the photovoltaic power system, this paper offers a design direction, emphasizing the relization of harmony through integrated planning with public buildings. The design guide proposed in this paper is expected to be the basic format to guide the design of efficient photovoltaic power generation system in the marine park.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model for Solar Radiation Forecasting towards Energy Efficient Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Solar radiation forecasting is developed for electricity utilization in buildings to improve energy efficiency. In this paper, we first compare different machine learning methods for single-step solar radiation prediction, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), long short-term memory (LSTM), gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT), random forest (RF) and Informer. Then, we propose a hybrid model for short-term solar irradiation prediction, which is composed of a random forest model and an Informer model. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed hybrid model for balancing the accuracy-complexity tradeoff.

articleTitle: Enhanced Integrated Inductor and Transformer Design for WPT LCC Resonant Converter System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents the method to minimize magnetic coupling from inductor coils in an enhanced integrated inductor and transformer design for an EV wireless charging DC/DC LCC resonant converter system. The enhanced integrated design is established from bottom to top as a thinner ferrite plate, a bipolar DD inductor coil, a thicker ferrite plate, a unipolar transmitter coil, EV wireless charging airgap, a unipolar receiver coil, a thicker ferrite plate, a bipolar DD inductor coil, and a thinner ferrite plate. The receiver and receiver side coils and ferrite plates of the same dimension are placed at a symmetrical distance around the airgap center. The receiver side DD inductor coil is rotated <tex>$\boldsymbol{90}^{0}$</tex> with respect to the transmitter side DD inductor coil. Ansys Maxwell 3D simulation results show that the enhanced design minimizes the magnetic coupling between DD inductor coils and their nearby transformer coils. The magnetic coupling between the transformer coils is slightly improved. The power capability and efficiency are both improved for the enhanced design. A full-order PLECS circuit model including the magnetic couplings of all coils is developed to validate the performance improvement in power capability and efficiency compared to the reference base design structure given in the literature.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization Based Multi-level Coordinated Scheduling Strategy for Energy Hub in Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Ensuring adequate energy supply and maximizing profitability are essential for energy hub(EH)-based Integrated Energy Service Providers (IESPs), which rely on optimal scheduling strategies for EH. However, multiple uncertainties exist in renewable energy output and multi-energy consumers. In addition, the energy prices in the day-ahead and real-time spot market are different and difficult to forecast, which brings additional uncertainty, making the energy management of EH very complex and difficult. To address this problem, we propose a robust optimization based multi-level coordinated scheduling strategy for energy hub in spot market. The first level is the day-ahead decision-making stage, where accurate information about the uncertainty distribution may not be available, so the strategy considers the worst-case, secures energy supply, and pre-purchases power in the day-ahead market. The subsequent levels are intra-day decision-making stages where multiple uncertainties are gradually revealed. In addition, according to the real-time electricity price, multiple stages within the strategy cooperate with each other, which can not only take into account the future uncertainties, but also offset the real-time uncertainties by adjusting the scheduling decisions made by the previous stages. In addition, the proposed optimal scheduling strategy was applied to a real simulation scenario. Taking the PJM business rules as an example, extensive simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness and advantages.
